items.text: Silent zero-defaults in data extraction (e.g. `bb.get('x', 0)`) fabricate plausible-looking numeric values when source data is missing or partial, producing downstream motion/delta claims that are entirely fabricated rather than absent.
items.note: Names the exact idiom bb.get('x',0) and the fabricated-delta consequence; checkable at write time.

items.text: The agent should never commit or push for protected projects (those in an explicit protected-repos registry); it must prepare the change, show the diff, and hand the commit to the user. Authorization to commit elsewhere does not extend to protected repos.
items.note: Concrete registry+handoff mechanic, but restates an existing standing rule verbatim.

items.text: When a user says a behavior is 'too noisy' or 'too aggressive', the correct response is to tune it down, not turn it off entirely — the complaint is a ceiling on intensity, not a removal mandate.
items.note: Real calibration insight (tune vs remove) but names no hook, threshold, or artifact.

items.text: User reassurance ('I trust you', 'that's fine') is not authorization to remove safeguards, gates, or confirmations — it is social comfort, not a blanket removal mandate.
items.note: Sharp distinction, zero concreteness — no surface, no example gate it applies to.

items.text: When a task list has not been updated across many turns but significant editing has occurred, the list has drifted from reality and must be reconciled before stopping — completed work marked done, new work added, in-progress set correctly.
items.note: Reconcile-before-stop is checkable, but 'many turns' is unquantified and duplicates f88fb5.

items.text: When a feature unexpectedly requires adding a new library or dependency, the agent should surface this constraint to the user and offer a within-existing-dependency alternative first rather than proceeding with the addition.
items.note: Ask-before-new-dep is standard practice; no named dep, ecosystem, or incident.

items.text: One-off inline styling for a UI element (instead of reusing the existing component hover/interactive patterns) is a signal that there is a gap in the UI kit — surface this observation rather than writing one-off CSS.
items.note: Inline-style-as-UI-kit-gap-signal is a non-obvious reframe; still no component or file named.

items.text: A fresh adversarial reviewer sub-agent reliably catches HIGH-severity bugs in code the main agent just wrote; dispatching one immediately after implementing a complex feature is a high-ROI verification step.
items.note: 'Fresh reviewer catches bugs' is near-tautology; 'reliably HIGH-severity' is unsupported.

items.text: Runtime dogfooding and live exercise catch bugs that a large test suite (99+ tests) misses; claimed correctness from test coverage alone is insufficient — actually running the affected path is a separate, necessary gate.
items.note: The 99+ tests detail grounds it, but this is the account's most-restated existing rule.

items.text: When a software dependency (model weights, binaries, large assets) must be downloaded at runtime and that download can time out or cause chaos, the correct design response is a pre-flight check that fails fast rather than allowing the feature to run in a broken half-downloaded state.
items.note: Pre-flight-fail-fast is a real design call; 'cause chaos' is vague filler.

items.text: For collaborative repos where multiple contributors work in parallel, establishing a named base branch at major feature checkpoints improves merge conflict isolation and lets parallel tracks merge independently rather than racing on the same target.
items.note: Standard branching advice; no repo, no observed conflict, no trigger for 'major checkpoint'.

items.text: Holding independent judgment and debating a proposed design decision rather than capitulating is explicitly valued; the user expects the agent to push back with evidence even after a reviewer or prior session recommended otherwise.
items.note: Heavily-affirmed preference, but stated as disposition with no at-decision check.

items.text: Config tools that perform validation only at parse time (not at write time) can silently break unrelated features when a required field is missing; always verify the full config profile loads correctly after editing, not just the targeted field.
items.note: Parse-time-vs-write-time validation gap is specific; 'reload the full profile' is runnable.

items.text: When multiple agents run in parallel on the same codebase, they must pre-negotiate task ownership via IPC before starting work; overlapping claims without coordination produces muddy, conflicting edits that the user has to untangle.
items.note: Names IPC pre-negotiation; exact duplicate of 3af60d09 — dedup failure counts against it.

items.text: A task list that accumulates many edits without corresponding TaskUpdate calls drifts into uselessness; the stop hook catching this after 20 edits and 8 turns confirms the failure mode is real and recurring.
items.note: 20 edits / 8 turns / hook-fired is real telemetry; the lesson itself is already canon.

items.text: The user prefers a breadth-first v1 pass across all surfaces before deep-diving into polish, validation, or improvement on individual items; pausing a sweep to perfect one area while others are unbuilt is the wrong priority order.
items.note: Breadth-first-v1 ordering is a genuine user preference; no surface or threshold named.

items.text: When sending IPC replies from a shell command, backticks and special characters in the message body get consumed by the shell and produce zero-byte or corrupted messages; quote the body carefully or use a here-string.
items.note: Backticks eat the body, zero-byte messages, here-string fix — mechanically reproducible.

items.text: In long parallel multi-agent sessions, writing a mini checkpoint after each discrete phase lets successor sessions restore context cheaply rather than rescanning the full codebase.
items.note: Checkpoint-per-phase is standing practice here; 'discrete phase' left undefined.

items.text: When building an access-gate system, unrecognized commands must default to DENY, not ALLOW; a default-allow fallback for unknown CLIs creates a bypass that renders the entire gate pointless.
items.note: Default-deny is security 101, but the unknown-CLI fallback case is concrete and checkable.

items.text: Patching a specific instance of a policy violation (e.g., adding one CLI to a fallback list) without fixing the underlying class of problem (the structural default) leaves the same vulnerability open at every future unknown case.
items.note: Instance-vs-class fix, anchored to the same allowlist incident; pairs with 138cca29.

items.text: The user prefers the agent to explore and ground itself in the existing codebase and surface a recommendation before touching code; jumping directly to edits without that grounding phase is a recurring correction.
items.note: 'Explore before editing' is a recurring correction here but stays a virtue statement.

items.text: Uncommitted agent edits to tracked files can be silently lost if the user commits or merges in a parallel operation; agent-made edits must be committed or explicitly stashed before handing control back to the user.
items.note: Non-obvious loss mode: parallel user commit eats uncommitted agent edits; clear handback gate.

items.text: The autocorrect hinter can corrupt bash command output text (e.g., mangling tool names into unrelated strings), making shell-captured output unreliable; use the Read tool to read file contents rather than trusting bash text.
items.note: Hinter mangling bash output is surprising and gives a direct tool substitution (Read over bash).

items.text: A Python exception class named 'NonRetryable' does not guarantee the framework skips retries; always read the error-handling code to confirm retry behavior rather than inferring it from the class name.
items.note: Named class NonRetryable vs actual retry behavior; instance of the read-the-code rule with teeth.

items.text: File Tools MCP `list_sheets`/`read_tabular` can fail on .xlsx files with a runtime error; keep a pandas fallback for spreadsheet reading tasks when the MCP path is unreliable.
items.note: Names the MCP calls, the file type, and the pandas fallback; reads as a logged failure.

items.text: Retrieval confidence is more trustworthy when computed from retrieval metrics (cosine score plus margin to the second result) than from the model's self-reported confidence, which tends to be overconfident.
items.note: Cosine + margin-to-second beats self-reported confidence — concrete and genuinely non-obvious.

items.text: When multiple agents need concurrent browser access, running duplicate dev servers on different ports gives each agent its own session without contention; the port-assignment overhead is lower than the coordination overhead of time-sharing one server.
items.note: Duplicate servers over time-sharing is a real tradeoff call; cost claim asserted, not measured.

items.text: Session-scoped stop hooks with explicit, verifiable completion conditions (e.g., 'must pass /ui-gripe before marking done') effectively prevent premature task closure in long autonomous sessions where the agent might self-declare success.
items.note: Session-scoped stop hook with a named gate (/ui-gripe) is an implementable mechanism.

items.text: Vercel's auth.json stores `expiresAt` in seconds since epoch, not milliseconds; an off-by-1000x error in expiry calculations causes valid tokens to appear immediately expired.
items.note: Vercel auth.json expiresAt in seconds, 1000x bug — exact, verifiable, unguessable.

items.text: When multiple agents work in parallel on the same codebase, they must pre-negotiate task ownership via IPC before starting work; overlapping claims without coordination produces muddy, conflicting edits that the user has to untangle.
items.note: Verbatim duplicate of 091b1300; novelty near zero as a distinct consolidated lesson.

items.text: The user prefers a breadth-first v1 pass across all surfaces before deep-diving into polish, validation, or improvements on individual items — pausing a sweep to perfect one area while others are unbuilt is the wrong priority order.
items.note: Real-sounding user preference but no surface named; 'breadth before depth' is near-platitude

items.text: When sending IPC replies from a shell command, backticks and special characters in the message body get consumed by the shell and produce zero-byte or corrupted messages; the body must be quoted carefully or passed via a here-string or temp file.
items.note: Concrete shell-quoting failure with named fix path; classic bug any shell user knows

items.text: A document drafted for the user may be shared directly with external business stakeholders; private conversational banter or dismissive commentary about those stakeholders must never appear in the document body, even when the surrounding chat contains it.
items.note: Reads like a real leak incident; near-duplicate of a09cd282, no doc/path named

items.text: When fixing a doc's voice by removing problematic content, do not overcorrect by stripping technical detail — target only the inappropriate content, not the technical framing; the fix should be scalpel-sized, not a full rewrite.
items.note: 'Scalpel not rewrite' is generic edit hygiene; overlaps 0865c79b

items.text: `rg -rn` is NOT 'recursive plus line-numbers' — the `-r` flag is `--replace`, which silently mangles output; always use `rg -n` for line numbers in recursive searches.
items.note: Exact flag, exact wrong belief, exact correction; strongest item in the set

items.text: When rewriting or refactoring an existing feature, inventory the current behavior first as a parity checklist and flag any removed behavior explicitly — don't let removals become silent byproducts of the rewrite.
items.note: Parity-checklist-before-rewrite is a runnable check but standard refactor doctrine

items.text: In a multi-agent setup where sessions are regularly context-cleared, each agent's checkpoint should record the peer agent's IPC alias so the next session can re-establish contact without requiring the user to re-introduce them.
items.note: Names checkpoint+IPC alias mechanics; duplicates e0fcf7bd almost verbatim

items.text: A sub-agent must not touch or drop guard mute-files; a dropped mute file disables the guard machine-wide for all concurrent sessions until manually removed, silently negating safety gates the main agent relies on.
items.note: Mute-file machine-wide blast radius is specific and non-obvious to a sub-agent

items.text: Code and docs can diverge between triage-time and edit-time; re-verify the specific file or function at the moment of writing the edit, not at the moment of planning it — the ground truth is the current file, not the earlier scan.
items.note: Re-verify-before-edit is baseline agent hygiene; no file/tool anchors it

items.text: A full-file rewrite makes the agent the author of all preserved content, including existing voice, conventions, and style — the entire file must be reviewed after the rewrite, not just the changed sections.
items.note: 'Rewrite makes you author of preserved content' is a genuinely useful reframe

items.text: In a multi-agent parallel workflow, each agent's task list can become stale; before starting any item, verify it has not already been completed by a peer agent rather than relying on the list state from session start.
items.note: Check-before-start against peer completion is a real parallel-workflow race

items.text: Advisory specs and skill docs only bind agents that read them at startup; to make a behavioral constraint effective across sub-agents and in-flight sessions, enforcement must be placed at the data-write layer (a hook, CLI gate, or schema check) rather than left as advisory text.
items.note: Advisory-vs-data-write-layer enforcement is sharp and matches a known rule lineage

items.text: When writing a document that will be shared externally, all internal banter, critique, and conversational framing about stakeholders must be stripped before the document is written — the agent must distinguish between what was said conversationally and what is safe to publish.
items.note: Duplicate of 367cb6df with vaguer framing; 'strip banter' without a check

items.text: Correcting a document's tone for its audience should adjust register only, not strip technical substance — overcorrecting toward accessible prose leaves engineers with an essay they will abandon for lacking implementation detail.
items.note: 'Register not substance' is a decent distinction; overlaps 1e686f47

items.text: When asking the user a decision question, include enough background and tradeoffs to make the question self-contained and answerable without additional follow-up; questions that force the user to ask for context before answering are a recurring friction point.
items.note: Self-contained questions is good practice but reads as generic comms advice

items.text: In multi-agent IPC sessions, unanswered peer queries must be replied to before the session ends; stop hooks will fire repeatedly for each unreplied message, indicating this is a mechanical obligation, not optional.
items.note: Stop-hook repetition as the tell makes this mechanically checkable

items.text: IPC message delivery should be confirmed by waiting for an actual round-trip reply from the peer, not by inspecting the sending agent's own logs; the user will reject log-based assurance and insist on a verified reply.
items.note: Send-log is not delivery proof; strong, but 6b8bd99e is the same lesson

items.text: In multi-agent sessions where context is regularly cleared, core-dump and checkpoint artifacts should explicitly capture peer agent IPC aliases and session IDs so successor sessions can re-establish connections without user intervention.
items.note: Near-verbatim duplicate of ec48740332; novelty discounted for redundancy

items.text: Task list hygiene degrades specifically during high-parallelism periods with many sub-agent completions; the task list must be explicitly reconciled after a burst of sub-agent work, not only at session boundaries.
items.note: Pinpoints WHEN task lists rot (post-fanout burst), not just that they do

items.text: The user prefers the agent to batch sequential work and only halt at genuine decision points or critical reviews, not at every short distance for lightweight go-aheads that force the user to context-switch repeatedly.
items.note: Genuine user preference but stated as vibe; duplicate of 464e86ec

items.text: Interactive input MCP tools and structured-choice prompts cannot be used when the user is in TUI fullscreen mode; the user cannot select options and must reject and answer in prose, so any structured input in that context will silently fail.
items.note: TUI fullscreen silently breaks structured-input MCP; specific and unguessable

items.text: Small fast models (e.g. gemini-3.5-flash) can match or outperform flagship models on closed-set classification tasks while costing significantly less; default model selection should not assume that harder tasks always require larger models.
items.note: Named model + task class; 'closed-set classification' is the load-bearing scope

items.text: Establishing a shared nomenclature or vocabulary document as a deliverable alongside an implementation plan helps validate cross-agent consistency and gives both agents and reviewers a stable reference for terminology during execution.
items.note: Shared-vocabulary-doc-helps reads as invented process wisdom, no check implied

items.text: When dispatching gemini sub-agents for large-scale transcript or corpus analysis, running a small test dispatch first before committing to the full fleet reduces wasted cost on prompt or tool errors that only surface at scale.
items.note: Smoke-test one dispatch before the fleet: cheap, concrete, gate-shaped

items.text: When verifying IPC message delivery, wait for an actual round-trip reply from the peer rather than inspecting the sending agent's own logs or send-side telemetry — a successful send does not prove the message arrived or was acted on.
items.note: Duplicate of 9a43dcfe with better rationale; redundancy caps novelty

items.text: In multi-agent sessions, the user should not have to repeatedly give plain go-aheads for short-distance progress; batch sequential work into autonomous runs and halt only at genuine decision points, blocking reviews, or missing user input.
items.note: Duplicate of 4010cebb; names halt conditions slightly better, still vague

items.text: When proposing names for packages, repos, or identifiers within the same organization, always default to a consistent naming scheme — suggesting diverging names across sibling artifacts in the same namespace is wrong without an explicit reason.
items.note: Consistent naming within a namespace is an assumption, not a lesson

items.text: CLI authentication commands (e.g. cloud provider logins) require an interactive terminal and cannot be automated; flag this to the user up front and hand off the auth step rather than attempting it and failing.
items.note: Interactive-auth cannot be automated; useful hand-off trigger, widely known

items.text: In multi-agent IPC setups where sessions are cleared periodically, registered aliases become stale after the owning session restarts; fall back to bare sessionId addressing for reliable delivery rather than trusting previously-registered aliases.
items.note: Stale alias after restart, fall back to sessionId — precise failure and remedy

items.text: When a sub-agent fleet hits API errors mid-run, salvage all finished work and re-dispatch only the failed agents rather than restarting the entire fleet.
items.note: Salvage-and-redispatch is concrete; already codified as a standing rule

items.text: When the user wants broad review coverage over a large surface, a fleet of lower-cost agents covering more items is preferable to fewer high-cost agents; the user values coverage and total number of findings over per-finding depth.
items.note: Real preference but no threshold for 'large surface'; fleet-vs-depth tradeoff stated vaguely

items.text: Keying each result in a batch job by (judge + item + discriminating labels) enables resuming mid-run on abort or API error without re-paying already-completed work — build resumable caches for expensive fan-out jobs.
items.note: Names concrete cache key composition; resumable-cache idea is standard engineering though

items.text: Dispatching gemini sub-agents to scan historical session transcripts is an effective recovery pattern when the current session has lost context about prior task state or accumulated feedback across many past sessions.
items.note: Specific lane+corpus pairing; reads like a real recovery episode

items.text: macOS ships without `timeout` or `gtimeout`; wrapping long-running scripts in a shell timeout on macOS silently orphans child processes and does not actually cap execution — use the script's own async timeout mechanism instead.
items.note: Concrete macOS trap with silent-failure mechanism; matches known shell.md finding

items.text: The Task tool must be updated incrementally throughout active work, not only at major milestones; allowing many edits to accumulate without reflecting them in the task list causes the live status view to drift and confuses both the user and future turns.
items.note: Restates existing todo-discipline rule; near-duplicate of 9cc1f4ee

items.text: When proposing names for packages, repos, or identifiers within the same organization, always default to a consistent naming scheme across sibling artifacts — suggesting diverging names in the same namespace without an explicit justification draws immediate pushback.
items.note: 'Be consistent in naming' is near-platitude; pushback detail is the only grounding

items.text: A sent IPC message is not confirmed until an actual round-trip reply arrives from the peer; inspecting send-side logs, send telemetry, or the sending agent's own turn output does not prove the message was received or acted on.
items.note: Sharp falsification rule: send-side logs never prove receipt; testable at decision point

items.text: While waiting for a peer agent to send information over an IPC channel, the agent should not repeatedly nudge the user for context or status updates — ask once, then wait for the real message rather than turning the user into a polling proxy.
items.note: Ask-once-then-wait is concrete; clearly from a real user irritation

items.text: Expressing concern about context window pressure when the session is well under half full reads as unnecessary anxiety to the user and should be suppressed — context warnings are appropriate only when actually approaching limits.
items.note: Matches the S3 stale-mental-model atone; 'well under half' is a soft threshold

items.text: Git branch state captured at session start can silently drift during the session; always re-read current branch state immediately before any branch-sensitive operation rather than relying on the value observed at session open.
items.note: Generic re-read-state-before-side-effect; already CLAUDE.md doctrine

items.text: Running an adversarial review pass against the agent's own synthesis documents (design proposals, plans, specs) catches motivated reasoning that self-review within the same context misses — independent skeptic framing on your own output is a reliable quality gate.
items.note: Adversarial self-review is standard practice; no concrete trigger or artifact named

items.text: When prompting the gemini lane, avoid `@`-prefixed package names or scoped identifiers directly in the prompt body — the CLI parses them as image-attach tokens and silently corrupts the intended text.
items.note: Exact CLI parsing gotcha (@ = image-attach); unguessable, clearly lived

items.text: When sending IPC messages between peer agents, the agent must verify the peer alias maps to the intended recipient by checking live peer IDs before sending — a descriptive alias name does not guarantee it identifies the correct session.
items.note: Concrete pre-send check against live peer IDs; alias-is-not-identity is real

items.text: During autonomous multi-turn work sessions, the task list must be updated after each logical unit of work rather than batching updates at session end — allowing the task list to drift from actual progress renders the live status surface useless.
items.note: Duplicate of 719d2e98; both restate existing todo-discipline rule

items.text: Shared UI elements such as navigation shells must be implemented from a single shared source component, not replicated per-page, so that all authenticated pages remain consistent without manual propagation.
items.note: DRY-for-shared-components is textbook; no project specifics

items.text: When resuming work after a significant project phase, verify that planning and handoff documents are current before working from them — superseded plans silently redirect effort onto stale tracks when the living state has moved on.
items.note: Stale-plan hazard is real but 'verify docs are current' lacks a concrete check

items.text: When working in a shared local repository with concurrent sibling sessions, commits created by those sessions should be identified and left alone rather than absorbed or pushed — ownership of a commit determines who publishes it.
items.note: Concurrent-sibling-session commit ownership is genuinely non-obvious; env-specific

items.text: When a hook has a high fire-rate but zero conversions, verify the hook is attached to the correct event type before attributing the failure to implementation — an event type mismatch means the hook fires on unintended triggers while the intended events are never caught.
items.note: High-fire/zero-conversion → check event-type binding first; sharp diagnostic

items.text: When a component returns no data, downstream derivation logic must emit an empty or uncertain result rather than converting the absence into a fabricated negative claim; treating an empty result as evidence of non-existence produces false negatives that are indistinguishable from real negative evidence.
items.note: Empty≠negative-evidence is a real trap; phrased abstractly, no concrete site

items.text: When presenting a list of deferred decision items to the user, each item must include the exact prior decision or constraint and concrete options; items without that context force a follow-up round-trip before the user can answer and are experienced as an incomplete handoff.
items.note: Concrete handoff contract (prior constraint + options); duplicates b1fd875f

items.text: When a list page is missing pagination and sibling list pages in the same session already display the paginated pattern, the agent should recognise and apply that pattern rather than treating each page in isolation; in-session context that directly proves the pattern is available evidence the agent must use.
items.note: Sibling-page pattern reuse; verbatim duplicate of 1afa5f53

items.text: A function return type annotation that silently diverges from the actual return arity (e.g., annotated as 2-tuple but returning 3-tuple) is invisible without a configured static type checker and will crash callers at runtime; projects without mypy or pyright have no backstop and are especially vulnerable to this class of bug.
items.note: Concrete arity-drift example; second clause states the obvious about missing typecheckers

items.text: Adding a new parameter to a cached function changes the cache key, causing all existing cache entries to become stale on the next run; before making this change silently, surface the one-time cache-flush implication to the user and ask whether to accept it or exclude the new parameter from the key.
items.note: New param → cache-key change → surface the flush cost; non-obvious and checkable

items.text: When a test lab or pipeline has long-lived caches, re-running it after a code change exercises the cache layer rather than the changed code; confirming a code change requires a cache-bust parameter or explicit cache invalidation before treating re-run results as evidence the fix works.
items.note: Cache-replay masquerading as verification; strong decision-point check

items.text: When a system distinguishes between multiple failure modes using different fields (e.g., partial-failure writes to field A while error-failure writes to field B), guards that only check one field silently pass the other failure mode through as a success; all failure-mode fields must be included in any guard that blocks downstream derivation.
items.note: Guard checks field A, failure-mode B slips through; concrete and generalizes well

items.text: Hardcoded character-length filters on domain strings (minimum word length, substring count thresholds) silently exclude legitimate short values from the real data population; filter constants must be validated against the actual corpus before being committed.
items.note: Validate filter constants against the real corpus; concrete silent-exclusion mechanism

items.text: When the user reports a UI component inconsistency on one page (sidebar, drawer, modal shell), the fix must be applied to all pages using that component simultaneously; treating it as a single-page fix while sibling pages still use incompatible variants is a failure the user experiences as a missed-obvious pattern.
items.note: Instance-vs-class fix, well grounded in user pushback; overlaps literal-request-over-intent

items.text: When a list page lacks pagination and other list pages in the same codebase already implement it, the agent must apply the pagination pattern without being explicitly told; the sibling-page pattern is available in-session evidence that must be used.
items.note: Duplicate of 770a52cc with near-identical wording; dedup failure

items.text: When presenting deferred decision items to the user, each item must include the exact prior decision or constraint plus concrete selectable options; items without that context force a follow-up round-trip before the user can act.
items.note: Duplicate of f9a58112; same handoff-completeness rule restated

items.text: In long-running multi-agent sprints, individual sub-agents hitting session limits can silently block orchestration; the coordinating agent should detect sub-agent session exhaustion in idle notifications and surface it to the user immediately rather than waiting for a timeout.
items.note: Sub-agent session exhaustion silently stalls orchestration; specific idle-notification check

items.text: Strong frustration language from the user ('idiot', expletives) is a high-confidence signal that the agent missed a pattern that was already established and visible in the existing codebase — the error is almost always about failing to read sibling context, not about intent misunderstanding.
items.note: Frustration-to-cause mapping is a bold claim with no mechanism; 'almost always' is unfalsifiable

items.text: When a UI standardization request arrives as a list of issues across multiple pages, the agent should sweep ALL pages that use the affected component, not only the pages named in the user's message — the named examples are a sample, not an exhaustive scope.
items.note: Named-examples-are-a-sample is checkable, but restates the standard intent-over-literal rule

items.text: Heartbeat/wake monitors in autonomous long-running sessions should verify remaining session budget before continuing work and self-terminate when budget is nearly exhausted rather than starting new work that will be cut off mid-flight.
items.note: Concrete to heartbeat monitors; 'nearly exhausted' has no threshold to check against

items.text: When the agent pauses mid-task without surfacing a reason, the user must ask why, consuming a check-in round-trip; agents should explicitly state the stopping condition (blocker, phase boundary, question needed) before halting execution.
items.note: State-your-stopping-condition is sound but generic politeness advice

items.text: CSS utility class names used in implementations should be confirmed as present in the project's actual stylesheet or framework configuration before use; names that look like valid defaults may not be available in a project using a custom subset.
items.note: Grep the stylesheet before using a utility class — a real, runnable pre-write check

items.text: Hard-stopping on a genuine quality or safety concern even when the user explicitly pushes for completion velocity is correct and affirmed; the user values that the agent does not silently accept known risks under schedule pressure.
items.note: Virtue statement; no trigger, no check, no named concern class

items.text: The absence of standard tooling such as linting, CI checks, or type enforcement in a project may be a deliberate decision to ship first and standardize later; the agent should probe whether a missing tool is an oversight or an intentional deferral before suggesting its addition.
items.note: Missing-tooling-may-be-deliberate is genuinely non-default; probe step is vague

items.text: In multi-agent workflows where one agent waits on a sibling for input, the user prefers the waiting agent to set an explicit time-to-live and proceed autonomously rather than blocking indefinitely, prioritizing pipeline velocity over synchronization completeness.
items.note: TTL-then-proceed is a real preference, but no TTL value given

items.text: When the user makes manual corrections and asks the agent to derive a heuristic from them, the deliverable is a general sweep rule extracted from the class of changes, not a catalogue of individual edits; pattern extraction is the goal, not change summarization.
items.note: Deliverable-is-a-rule-not-a-changelog is a crisp misread this catches

items.text: When an agent edits source files and then claims success using words like 'done', 'works', 'fixed', or 'passing' without actually executing the changed code path, it constitutes a false completion claim — type-checking, linting, and collecting tests are not substitutes for running the code.
items.note: Well-grounded but already a hard rule + Stop hook; zero novelty

items.text: When the user orchestrates multiple parallel agents with distinct roles, each agent should stay within its assigned workload and coordinate via inter-agent messaging rather than picking up tasks assigned to the peer agent.
items.note: Stay-in-lane for parallel agents; already standard dispatch hygiene

items.text: When the user provides UI feedback via screenshots repeatedly across multiple turns, the preferred workflow is direct visual analysis and immediate implementation of visible changes without asking for clarification on visually obvious issues.
items.note: Don't-ask-on-visually-obvious is a real preference inversion of the cautious default

items.text: When a standardization or normalization task spans multiple similar items (pages, components), the agent tends to complete it partially without creating discrete tasks for remaining items, leaving incomplete work the user must discover and flag themselves.
items.note: Partial-sweep-without-tasks; near-duplicate of 8331f4f6 with a task-tool twist

items.text: Under high edit velocity (many file changes per turn), the agent's task list drifts from actual work done — the discipline that holds at low throughput is the first to slip when editing pace accelerates, requiring external hooks to force reconciliation.
items.note: Velocity-degrades-task-discipline is an interesting claim but implies no check

items.text: When the user asks for a specific UI feature, they often explicitly want a 'pluggable general capability' usable across multiple routes or surfaces — the agent defaults to implementing the single instance without flagging the extensibility question or offering a registration pattern.
items.note: Flag-the-extensibility-question cuts against the standing anti-speculation rule; useful tension

items.text: The user places high priority on navigation feel when implementing URL-synced tab state and expects the agent to proactively evaluate whether path params will cause noticeable latency before committing to that approach.
items.note: Path-params vs latency on URL-synced tabs is narrowly concrete and non-obvious

items.text: When implementing a UI shell component (sidebar, drawer, modal) on one page, the agent must audit all sibling pages for the same component before writing any code — implementing per-page variants of a globally-shared shell is a systematic error, not an isolated miss.
items.note: Audit sibling pages before coding a shell component — concrete pre-write gate

items.text: When a list page is missing pagination and sibling list pages in the same codebase already display the paginated pattern, the agent must apply the same pagination before returning — treating each page in isolation when the pattern is already proven nearby is a systematic miss.
items.note: Pagination parity with sibling list pages; checkable, but same family as 92535999

items.text: When presenting deferred decision items to the user, each item must include the exact prior decision or constraint and at least two concrete options; items without that context force an unnecessary follow-up round-trip and are experienced as an incomplete handoff.
items.note: Prior-constraint + 2 options per deferred item is a countable format spec

items.text: When a sub-agent hits a credential or auth block that is outside its own scope to fix, it should surface the exact command the user needs to run and hold — not attempt workarounds — so the human can unblock it in one action.
items.note: Surface the exact unblock command and hold, no workarounds — clear at a decision point

items.text: PR comments and inline docstrings should be stripped to the minimum non-obvious WHY; essay-length comments on small or self-evident changes are treated as noise and removed, not appreciated as thoroughness.
items.note: Comment minimalism already canon in comments.md and memory; restatement

items.text: When the user says 'do not pick stupid fields' or similar judgment constraints, the agent must apply genuine editorial judgment — only surfacing fields with clear user value — rather than enumerating every technically-editable field.
items.note: 'Apply genuine judgment' is a restatement of the ask, not a criterion for which fields

items.text: When a session hits its usage limit while coordinating multiple sub-agents via IPC, sub-agents are left waiting without a response; the architecture should anticipate this by having sub-agents self-report idle state so the orchestrator can re-queue them on resume.
items.note: IPC deadlock on usage limit is real; prescribes architecture, not a session-time check

items.text: When implementing a UI shell component (sidebar, drawer, modal) on one page, the agent builds per-page variants instead of a single globally-shared component, requiring the user to explicitly correct this systematic error multiple times in the same session.
items.note: Near-verbatim duplicate of 92535999 stated as failure rather than rule

items.text: When a list page is missing standard pagination while sibling list pages already implement it, the agent leaves the gap uncorrected and waits for the user to point it out explicitly.
items.note: Duplicate of de32a41d, restated as a complaint with no prescribed check

items.text: When presenting deferred decision items to the user, the agent omits the prior decision context and concrete options, forcing the user to ask a follow-up question before they can act.
items.note: Duplicate of 564698a2 minus the two-options criterion; strictly weaker

items.text: When a sub-agent hits a credential or authentication block outside its own scope, surfacing the exact command the user must run and then holding (not attempting workarounds) unblocks the human in one action.
items.note: Duplicate of aa9f2ddc phrased as affirmation; same content

items.text: When a main orchestrator session hits its usage limit while sub-agents are waiting on IPC responses, sub-agents are left blocked indefinitely; the architecture must anticipate this by having sub-agents self-report idle state so they can be re-queued on resume.
items.note: Duplicate of c3df6b32 with orchestrator framing; no added check

items.text: When designing a new UI component variant or layout, the agent proceeds directly to implementation without showing the user a visual mock or sample first, losing the opportunity for early feedback before code is written.
items.note: Show a mock before coding a new UI variant — actionable, though scope of 'new variant' is fuzzy

items.text: When implementing any UI drawer or sidebar component on one page, the agent must audit every page in the application that could trigger the same component before writing any code — per-page variants of a globally-shared shell are an architectural error, not a scoped fix.
items.note: Third restatement of the drawer/sidebar audit rule; grounded but redundant
